items.title: Live: Trump says US will 'shoot and ‌kill any ​boat' laying mines in ​the ‌Strait of ⁠Hormuz

items.title: It's a very bad time to be a baby boomer, politically speaking
items.description: The Albanese government is reading the room when it comes to intergenerational equity ahead of the May 12 budget.

items.title: 'Finfluencers' suspected of giving unlawful advice hit with warning notices
items.description: The warning notice to the so-called "finfluencers" relates to suspected provision of unlicensed financial advice, including promoting claims of guaranteed returns.

items.title: The NDIS gave participants their lives back. Now they fear what's to come
items.description: NDIS participants set up their lives around the scheme's rules. But now the rules are changing and they fear what lies ahead.

items.title: Plan to end NDIS 'wild west' will flip rules on their head for providers
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler will end the practice of handwritten invoices, providers without qualifications and a "let it rip" market of profiteering operators. But the sector warns it must be navigated carefully to avoid driving away legitimate operators or accidentally leaving out providers helping people with complex, individualised needs.

items.title: Watchdog to audit US Department of Justice over Epstein files
items.description: The audit follows months of controversy over censorship, missed deadlines and the publication of survivors' details.

items.title: Warnings of power price rises, missed renewable targets under proposed tax
items.description: The treasurer says changes to capital gains tax for foreign investors is a clarification, but experts say it could dampen investment.

items.title: Charts explain why fertiliser prices aren't coming down anytime soon
items.description: Farmers around the world are going to be paying more for one of their most important inputs, fertiliser. Here are four charts that explain why.

items.title: Australia's fuel supply: Where things stand and what we are watching
items.description: The week's most important fuel news, analysis and pricing information.

items.title: Viva Energy boss says more refineries needed for secure fuel supply
items.description: The Viva Energy refinery provides about 10 per cent of Australia's fuel. Its chief, Scott Wyatt, chats to Alan Kohler about the company's future in the wake of the Geelong fire.

items.title: 'This is now terminal': UK braces for prospect of sixth PM in seven years
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer, who led Labour to a landslide general election victory in July 2024, has become so unpopular that even some colleagues are framing his demise as a case of not if, but when.

items.title: Ancient fossils reveal when the iconic Twelve Apostles formed
items.description: An analysis of tiny fossils of sea creatures found in rock samples around the Port Campbell region in south-western Victoria has refined our understanding of how the Twelve Apostles formed.

items.title: 'Sad for us': Hannah Clarke's parents step back from advocacy
items.description: After their daughter and three grandchildren were murdered, Sue and Lloyd Clarke began a charity to improve awareness of coercive control. Now they've decided they need to step back for their own health.

items.title: Why China is recruiting fishermen to 'maintain presence' — not to fish
items.description: Off China's southern coast, hundreds of fishing boats sit idle. The crews aren't there to fish, but rather to "maintain presence" as part of a shadowy, state-funded fleet.

items.title: Jane Fonda was in her 40s when she changed the way we exercise
items.description: In the 1980s, the fitness industry as we know it was just getting started. One of the most important people in developing the way we exercise today was Jane Fonda, who released a best-selling aerobics video in 1982.

items.title: The advice Mackenzie Arnold gave her heir apparent, Chloe Lincoln
items.description: The A-League Women finals kick off this weekend, with Brisbane to make its first appearance in five years.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Trump's eleventh-hour announcement, a disabled bird and a speedy humanoid robot
items.description: It's Friday, and that means it's time to test your news knowledge from the past seven days. Were you paying attention this week?

items.title: Now James Valentine is gone, I'll let you in on the secret of his success
items.description: Children grew up with him, adults grew old with him, he kept us connected to our city, the world and each other. James helped us make sense of life and gave us permission to laugh at the absurdity of it all — and ourselves.

items.title: 'They deserve death': Officer used police system to monitor wife
items.description: Text messages read in court set out how a Tasmania Police officer monitored his wife's movements, including via an internal dispatching system, as part of a 15-month family violence matter.

items.title: The legacy of once-banned soldiers that hides in plain sight
items.description: Thousands of Indian soldiers served alongside Anzac forces at Gallipoli, leaving their legacy in the "puggaree" — a traditional Indian headwrap that was adapted to adorn the slouch hats worn by the Australian army.

items.title: Which states get a public holiday for Anzac Day?
items.description: Anzac Day is observed on April 25 every year. This year that date falls on a Saturday, but that doesn't mean a long weekend for everyone.

items.title: Documents reveal fresh details about Roberts-Smith’s overseas moving plans
items.description: Police were concerned war veteran Ben Roberts-Smith was attempting to move overseas and possibly to Singapore or Spain, court documents reveal.

items.title: Genesis Owusu goes out of his way to connect with fans — and detractors
items.description: Genesis Owusu today releases his new track Life Keeps Going from his upcoming third album Redstar Wu & the Worldwide Scourge, as he encourages engagement with people who don't agree with his political views.

items.title: After tornado warnings and midnight matches, Wallaroos are ready for NZ
items.description: Having survived the threat of tornadoes during their US tour, the Wallaroos are enjoying a distraction-free build-up to their Anzac Day Test against New Zealand.

items.title: Curnow kicks a bag in big Swans win as Bulldogs star suffers horror fall
items.description: Sydney's hold on top spot is strengthened by a 66-point win over the Western Bulldogs, whose injury woes continue.
